one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 results are not yet on the IR calendar as of Oct 2, but vendors estimate Oct 29 and past prints were Oct 30 2025 and Oct 31 2024, before the open. The window ends Fri Oct 30, so the print is ~85-90% likely to land inside it. The FOMC meets Oct 27-28 after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00%, and the TCEQ owes the Texas governor its compliance report on the data-center permit halt by Oct 19. Earnings-day moves have been large both ways (+17.3% Q2-26, about -2.5% Q3-25). The beat history argues for a little upside; a rate-sensitive 34x multiple and a 'beat but de-rate' reaction argue for downside. I have no directional edge, so I keep a near-symmetric lognormal centred at $664 with sigma 14% (12.6% base monthly vol plus an earnings premium). This is unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of 30x Oct-2027 NTM adj EPS of $21.6 ($648, 50%), 19x NTM EBITDA of $5.3B less $5.9B net debt ($622, 30%) and a 3% FCF yield on 2027E FCF of $2.7B ($590, 20%), giving ~$630. I cut the 2027 EPS haircut from 3% to 1.5% because backlog grew +49% YoY, raised net debt to $5.9B, and kept the 30x multiple because of the September Fed hike.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus $19.64 cut ~1.5% (was 3%). Backlog +49% YoY ($35.8B to $53.4B) with NiSource mostly still outside it supports consensus. But Technology & Load Centers grows 220-240% in 2026 from ~10% of 2025 revenue, which makes it ~24% of 2026 revenue by my arithmetic, so Texas and other permit pauses still bear on 2027 large-load work.
+15.5% on $19.35: the low half of management's 15-20% long-term adj EPS CAGR, nudged up from 15% because 12-month backlog grew +61%

Currently ~34-35x NTM (TIKR, Sep 24), down from ~50x in June. JPM, BMO and Benchmark downgraded on valuation, Piper trimmed its target to $714 on Sep 28, and the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 with one more hike signalled. Together these argue for a de-rating to ~30x, still above the pre-AI-cycle multiple.

bear.story: AI and data-center digestion. Hyperscaler 2027 capex growth falls toward or below UBS's ~25%. Texas extends its permit halt past the mid-December audit and other states copy it, hitting Technology & Load Centers (now ~24% of 2026 revenue) and pushing NiSource and large-load awards to the right. The Fed's hiking cycle de-rates high-multiple names. NTM EPS slips to ~$18.5, the multiple falls to ~22x (contractor peer level), and debt-funded M&A plus contract-asset build hurt cash conversion.

base.story: Guidance is met, the Q3 print is a modest beat, and 2027 adj EPS lands around $19.3-19.8 with backlog supporting it. The multiple drifts from ~34x to ~30x NTM under higher rates, so earnings growth roughly offsets the de-rating and the stock ends near spot.

bull.story: 25%+ beats continue, NiSource and other megaprojects enter backlog and ramp in 2H27, labor-scarcity pricing holds, and the Texas audit clears the permit queue. NTM EPS reaches ~$24 and the multiple holds at ~38x despite rates.

thesis_break_reason: $470 is ~24x 2027 consensus adj EPS (~$19.6-19.7) and ~29% below spot. The market would likely only accept that multiple if expected earnings were falling: a 2027 guide below consensus, a sequential backlog decline, NiSource or large-load programs slipping out of 2027, or a hyperscaler/utility capex retrenchment. Ordinary 44%-vol drift alone is unlikely to take it there. I set it slightly above the supervisor's $455 because Technology & Load Centers is ~24% of 2026 revenue, not ~10%, so a data-center shock would show up in guidance sooner.

reasoning: Round 2. I started from my round-1 work and the supervisor's fact-checks. Accepted: backlog grew +49% YoY ($35.84B to $53.44B; 12-month backlog +61%) with most of NiSource still excluded. That weakens the case for cutting 2027 EPS, so I halved my haircut to ~1.5% (2027 $19.35). Net debt is ~$5.9B (424B5 pro forma $5.6B plus Enerfab and ongoing M&A). The Sep 16 Fed hike supports keeping a 30x target multiple instead of letting the stronger backlog lift it. The Polymarket recession odds come from a thin (~$9.7k) market, so I treat them as sentiment only. Disputed: the supervisor says Technology & Load Centers is ~10% of 2026 revenue. The company's table gives ~10% of 2025 revenue growing 220-240% in 2026, with Utility ~50% (+20-25%), Generation ~25% (+10-15%) and three ~5% segments at 0-10%. That implies tech is ~24% of 2026 revenue, partly from acquisitions (Dynamic Systems, Tri-City, Phalcon). So direct data-center exposure is larger than either of us stated in round 1, and the Texas halt (now covering all state permits, TCEQ report due Oct 19, audit mid-December) remains a genuine skeptic risk. That is why I keep a small haircut and a left-tail component. New skeptic evidence: Piper trimmed its target to $714 (Sep 28). I found no new short report, rating action or post-June large insider sale; credit is still Baa3 positive. Valuation: P/E $648, EV/EBITDA $622, FCF yield $590, blended ~$630. Scenario mean ~$665 (25% $410 / 50% $660 / 25% $930). Ladder: a mixture of 88% lognormal (median $675, sigma 0.36) and 12% crash (median $470, sigma 0.35), down from 15% crash weight given the backlog. Median ~$649, P(>=spot) 0.48 (round 1: 0.45). The 1-month view is unchanged: Q3 print and FOMC fall in the window with no edge. Limits: I used 6 searches/fetches. Consensus EPS still comes from aggregator snippets.
